result.rationale: The diff shows `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb. ERB's `<%= %>` applies HTML escaping (h), not JS string escaping, so a referer containing a backslash or closing quote would break the JS literal and the resize postMessage would never fire. The mechanism described is verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: Server data interpolated into an inline JS string literal in embed.html.erb (`'<%= request.referer %>'`) uses HTML escaping instead of JS escaping; a referer ending in `\` escapes the closing quote producing invalid JS so the resize postMessage never fires — should use j/json_escape or a data attribute

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb, the inline script calls parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>');. The ERB output is inserted directly into a single-quoted JavaScript string without JS escaping (Rails default escaping is HTML-oriented and will not escape backslashes/newlines, and may not prevent breaking out of the JS literal). A Referer header ending with a backslash (or containing an unescaped single quote/newline) would produce invalid JS, preventing the onload handler from running and the resize message from firing. Using j/json_escape or avoiding inline JS via a data attribute would fix it.
